## Body

Skill PRs (the pij skill's routes and SKILL.md) since 2026-11-09, what bit:

- `skill_verb_coverage` (`crates/cli/tests/skill_verb_coverage.rs`) checks every `pij ...` command printed in the community route and the templates against the leaf's own `--help`. It requires the flags of one of the leaf's `Usage:` lines. A form the verb accepts but Usage doesn't list fails as "a required flag is missing". On #209, `pij directory edit ... --add-rule` failed this way, because Usage lists only --set and --file. Write such forms in prose, and send the Usage gap to its code owner.
- Never put `a|b` alternatives inside a printed bash command. Run, it becomes a pipeline (#211 round 1, spoonbill). Use one valid value in the command and list the choices in prose after the block.
- The community route has a 100-line budget, raised to 110 in #201 (`harness/scripts/pij-skill-check.sh`), and it now sits at 109-110. Edit lines in place rather than adding; raise the budget only in the same PR, with a reason.
- C-numbered rulings (C23, C28, C30, C31...) aren't the skill's § C1-C12 conventions. Link a ruling on first use to where it's explained (the route heading or the docs/how/pij-rs-api.md section).
- F165 (#209): the pij/{prd,blueprint,workstream} schemas ship in `skills/pij/schemas/pij/`, byte-identical to `.dd/schemas/pij/`. pij-skill-check fails on drift, and biome.json skips that folder. When a schema changes, copy it there in the same PR.
- Output subjects are `<kind>:<name>`, at most 96 characters (a file is `file:<repo-relative path>`); wildcat's F156 refuses anything else.
- C34: two review rounds. Prepare the round 2 fix locally and push once, after the last verdict is written.
- Process: `just pr-freeze <pr>` runs in a worktree with no node_modules. The shared cargo target (fleet-194-role-templates/target) is often held for 30+ minutes, so pass `--timeout` to shared-build. If the target stays busy, rely on CI's rust-test (nextest runs skill_verb_coverage) and say so in the PR.
- Before writing a claim from a packet, check it against the code. On #201, a role's default_seat.model wasn't applied at spawn, and an --in-reply-to reply did mark a request answered.
